newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon cuts GM EPS view.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon cuts GM EPS view.

text.p: -- Salomon Brothers analyst Jack Kirnan cut his 1996 fourth quarter estimate for General Motors Corp to $0.50 a share from $1.00 a share.
-- Kirnan also cut his full year 1996 estimate to $5.30 a share from $5.80 a share.
-- Kirnan said he remains confident about 1997 full year estimate of $7.50 a share.

-- On Wednesday, General Motors told analysts it expects fourth quarter earnings of about $0.60 a share, falling below analysts' consensus estimates of $1.00 a share, according to analysts. GM cited higher incentives and advertising costs for new products, analysts said.
-- Salomon sees the current fourth quarter performance as "largely transitional."
-- Salomon reiterated its buy rating on the stock. Salomon said it "would be an aggressive buyer of the stock on any further weakness."
-- Several factors will hurt GM's fourth quarter. Salomon expects GM's SG&A costs will be up $400 million to $3.3 billion, or about $300 million higher than its original estimated.

-- Incentive spending in North America is running about $100 per unit higher than planned, at $700 per unit. However, this higher level is still below the spending of rivals Ford and Chrysler, Salomon said.
-- Equity earnings from subsidiaries will be lower than estimated due to higher credit losses at GMAC and tougher comparisons as at Isuzu and SAAB affiliates, Salomon said.
